value.rationale: The largest cardinality of an inclusion-minimal percolating seed set is a natural irredundancy invariant distinct from minimum seed size. The two cospectral, strongly regular graphs have equal minimum six but different largest irredundant sizes seven versus six; the Shrikhande exception is one geometrically recognizable 64-element orbit. The exact propagation-time census refines the distinction and has direct meaning for speed-sensitive seeding. This is a complete natural finite classification and not a claim about arbitrary networks.
